questions.q: Which pane lists every table and column in your model, for you to drag or check onto the canvas?
questions.explain: The Fields pane lists every table and column available in the loaded model. Checking a box or dragging a field builds a visual automatically.

questions.q: You've built a bar chart and want to turn it into a line chart without losing your field selections. Where do you do that?
options: Select the visual, then choose a different icon in the Visualizations pane
Delete the visual and start over in the Fields pane
questions.explain: Selecting a different visual icon in the Visualizations pane redraws the same underlying fields as a new chart type — no need to rebuild it.

questions.q: Which view shows every table in your model as boxes connected by relationship lines?
questions.explain: Model view lays out every table in the model and draws a line between any two tables that have a relationship — the subject of Chapter 4.

questions.q: Which view would you use to sanity-check the actual row-level values a DAX measure is producing?
questions.explain: Data view (also called Table view) shows the raw rows and columns of your model, plus a formula bar — the place to verify a measure or calculated column is producing the values you expect.

questions.q: Is hiding a report page a security measure?
options: No — anyone with edit access can still unhide and see it
Yes — hidden pages can never be viewed by anyone again
Only if the report is published to the Power BI service
Only if the page is also deleted
questions.explain: Hiding a page only affects what report readers see in the Power BI service's Reading view. It is not a security control — anyone with edit access can unhide it or see it in Edit view.
